aiExplanation: This code solves a **minimum cost path problem** from the top-left to bottom-right of a 2D grid. It works by sorting all grid cells by their cost values, then running up to **k+1 relaxation iterations**. In each iteration, it groups cells with identical costs together and propagates the **minimum accumulated cost** to all cells in each group. After that, it uses **dynamic programming** working backwards from the bottom-right corner (where the cost is 0) to calculate the cheapest way to reach every other cell by only moving right or down. This relaxation process repeats k times to explore different path possibilities, allowing the algorithm to find the globally optimal minimum cost to reach the top-left starting position. The final answer is the accumulated cost at position `[0][0]`.
